artworks.title: A Road in the Hills Near Dordrecht
artworks.medium: pen and black ink on wove paper mounted to paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image depicts a landscape viewed from a slightly elevated position. The horizon is high in the image, showing rolling hills extending into the distance. A path runs through the scene, lined by a wooden fence that continues into the landscape. The brushstrokes vary in technique with dense, dark lines in the foreground for texture and lighter, sketchier lines for depth. The color scheme is primarily monochromatic, with tan paper complementing black and grey ink tones, creating a classic and timeless look.

artworks.title: Studies of a Swan
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)

artworks.title: Swans in the Water
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two swans on the water. The drawing depicts the swans with simple, flowing lines. One swan is shown in a resting position with its wings folded, while the other seems to be preening or stretching its wings. The water is illustrated with light strokes to suggest reflection and movement.

artworks.title: Studies of a Man's Head
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This drawing is a sketch showing two profile views of a person's head and neck. On the left, the person is shown in a right-facing profile with their chin slightly tilted downward. Their eyes are closed and their expression is neutral. Their hair appears short and closely cropped to their head. On the right, the same person is seen in a left-facing profile with their chin slightly lifted and their eyes looking upward. In both profiles, they have deeply-set eyes, high cheekbones, arched eyebrows, a sharp nose, and full lips. Both of the sketches are near the top of the paper, and the background is plain.

artworks.title: Bacchus
artworks.medium: pastel over graphite with metallic paint on wove paper mounted to paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a person seated with relaxed posture and one leg crossed over the other. They have curly red hair, soft facial features, and a slight smile. The person is depicted mostly unclothed with a cloth around their waist, holding a rod in one hand and a cup in the other. In the background, another figure is pouring liquid into the cup. The scene is set against an ancient architectural backdrop with warm hues and a dark frame.

artworks.title: Study for "Astronomy"
artworks.medium: charcoal and graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing of a person seated in a kneeling position. The person has their head tilted back, face turned upward, closed eyes, and a serene expression. Their hair is covered by their clothing, which consists of draping robes. The person's hands are gently clasped in front of them. The background consists of a dark circle framing the figure. In the top right corner, there are faint handwritten labels with the names of several zodiac signs.

artworks.title: Lake Shore, Menaggio [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a calm body of water with a mountainous backdrop. The horizon aligns with the shore, fading into distant peaks. Two sailboats float on the water, one closer to us. On the shore, three figures and a rowboat are visible. The scene is depicted with soft pencil strokes, creating a tranquil atmosphere. The artwork uses shades of gray for a monochromatic palette, enhancing the peaceful and simple scene.

artworks.title: En route pour la pêche (Setting Out to Fish)
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Irving Moskovitz, 1976)
artworks.description: This drawing depicts a group of people standing together, most of them facing left. There appear to be four women wearing dresses and shawls with head coverings, all holding baskets. There are also two children walking with them. More people can be seen in the distance on the right, next to what looks like a fence. The ground beneath the central group is covered with some reflective puddles, and in the distance on the left is what looks like a shoreline with small sailboats floating on the water. The sky above is cloudy.

artworks.title: Ponte Panada, Fondamenta Nuove, Venice
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Mabel Stevens Smithers, 1952)
artworks.description: This painting shows buildings at the edge of a river or canal. On the left, a gondola with a canopy floats on top of the water, carrying a person in a hat. Behind the boat, a bridge arches over the water, leading to pale-red and cream-colored buildings in the distance. More boats can be seen along the shore on the right. The brushstrokes in the painting are loose and fluid, and color palette consists of soft blues, grays, browns, and ochres. The water reflects the soft colors of the boats and buildings, as well as the pale gray of the sky.

artworks.title: La difficulté d'arriver a une place
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an omnibus. The top section shows a crowded interior with passengers tightly packed. The lower section portrays the exterior where a conductor gestures at a person who has fallen to the ground while another clings onto the side of the omnibus.

artworks.title: Design for an Emblem of the State of South Carolina
artworks.medium: pen and black ink with wash on heavy wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring a large circular medallion with two distinct engraved figures, a bust adorned with laurels, a robed figure holding a staff, a uniformed figure with a musket, a cannon, and cannonballs.

artworks.title: Study of Apollo for "Apollo and the Muses"
artworks.medium: charcoal and graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body sketch of a standing male figure. The left arm is raised, and the right hand rests on the hip. The man's head is turned slightly to the right, with delicately sketched facial features and short, neatly groomed hair. The figure is depicted nude, highlighting the body's contours and musculature. The sketch is on paper with a light grid overlay for layout, with no background elements visible.

artworks.title: Landscape with Deer, North Carolina
artworks.medium: watercolor and gouache over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum exchange, through bequest of James Parmelee, 1965)

artworks.title: Pomegranate Fruit
artworks.medium: pen and black ink with watercolor over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1963)
artworks.description: The image shows a cluster of oranges hanging from a branch with several elongated leaves. The oranges are speckled in an orange-brown hue, and the leaves are greyish-green. Small white flowers resembling citrus blossoms are scattered among the oranges and leaves. The branch is positioned diagonally from the top left to the bottom right, against a light beige background.

artworks.title: Polling [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a side view of a wagon filled with hay. The horizon line is low, obscured by the tall stack of hay and a large structure. A road or path runs beside the wagon. The drawing is done with loose pencil strokes for texture. It is in monochrome with shades of grey and black on beige paper. Figures are included on the haystack and near the wooden structure. A tree with minimal foliage is on the right, and the sky is depicted with horizontal strokes.

artworks.title: Woman Watching Puppies
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a person standing against a wooden surface with one arm resting on top of the surface. They are wearing a long-sleeved garment with a vest and a long skirt. The person has short hair and their face is not entirely visible. Some fabric and boards are draped around them. Three small animals are in the foreground. The background is sparsely detailed, indicating a possible outdoor setting.

artworks.title: Female Nude
artworks.medium: charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Walter Shirlaw, wife of the artist, 1912)

artworks.title: Studies of Feet
artworks.medium: graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Walter Shirlaw, wife of the artist, 1912)
artworks.description: The image shows a detailed sketch of two feet and a lower leg. The drawing captures the feet from a slightly angled overhead view, showing realistic proportions and toes. The right foot is positioned with the toes pointing slightly upward. The lower leg, on the right side, shows muscle definition and a natural curvature. The illustration uses fine pencil lines to detail the anatomy and shadowing for a three-dimensional effect. There are no facial features, hair, or clothing shown in the image. The background is plain, focusing on the anatomical study.

artworks.title: Male Nude with Staff
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Walter Shirlaw, wife of the artist, 1912)
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body view of a nude male figure seen from the back. The person is in an upright position, leaning slightly forward with their left foot on the ground and the right leg bent, resting on a raised surface. Their left arm is extended upward, holding a vertical pole, while the right arm is bent at the elbow and resting on a rock or elevated area. The figure's head is turned slightly to the left, with shoulder-length wavy hair. No facial features are visible. The background is a landscape with rocks and textured ground. The sketch is monochrome with shading to highlight the figure's muscles and the surroundings.

artworks.title: Granada
artworks.medium: graphite and watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of the National Academy of Design, Katherine S. Drew Collection, 1954)
artworks.description: The image shows a path with two figures on horseback traveling away. In the background, there are hills or mountains, and to the left, there is a structure with a thatched roof among trees. The artwork features loose brushstrokes and pencil work with a subdued color palette of earthy tones and hints of red and pink.

artworks.title: Study for "Toning the Bell"
artworks.medium: brush and brown ink wash over graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Florence Heywood, 1968)
artworks.description: The image shows a partial body sketch of an older man playing the violin. The man is positioned facing slightly to the left with his upper body visible, and he holds a violin under his chin. His facial features are depicted with a wide-open mouth and a focused expression, and he has short hair. He wears a loose-fitting garment suggested by sketch lines. The man's hand is holding the violin bow, showcasing a dynamic pose as part of his performance. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Ruins of a Tavern, Petersburg, Virginia
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a high-angle view of a series of brick ruins, likely in an urban environment. The bricks vary in shades of brown and red. Trees are visible on the horizon against a sky transitioning from blue to peach. In the background, there are intact structures in muted grays and browns. Other buildings and spires are faintly visible in the distance. The brushstrokes are delicate, creating an atmospheric effect. Warm, earthy tones dominate the color palette. A woman in a dress with a shawl stands on a pathway among the ruins.

artworks.title: Cavaliers in Battle
artworks.medium: graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a cavalry charge with horses and riders in motion. The figures are detailed with lines and shading, showing movement and tension. One rider is mid-gallop on a rearing horse on the right, and another horse appears to have fallen in the lower section. The riders wear military attire and hold swords or sabers aloft. Sparse vegetation fills the background.

artworks.title: Ce qui nous prouve comme quoi il est ... inutile ...
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The drawing depicts several people in a theater or similar venue, with characters shown from the waist up. A central figure in a dark coat faces the viewer, surrounded by others wearing cloaks or shawls. One woman has an updo and long-sleeved attire. The background shows a blurred audience seated in rows indoors. Two top-hatted figures loom behind the group, and on the right, two men and one woman seem to be in motion. The setting suggests a busy social gathering with a focus on the central figures.
